**Orbweaver 1.0.6 adds automatic orb groups, hiding orbs, clickable chat links and re-opening OpenClaw conversations. It also carries a security fix for the link between machines, and a set of fixes for answering from the phone on narrow panes.**

## Security

- **An unpaired machine on your network can no longer read through the peer link.** In 1.0.5, an incoming connection was treated as trusted before its pairing was checked, so an unpaired client on the local network could have its mirror requests answered. Now frames are discarded until the connection's pairing is accepted. Connections that never finish their handshake are dropped after 15 seconds instead of being held open forever. Connections you dial out were not affected. **Everyone on 1.0.5 should upgrade.**

## What's new

- **Group orbs automatically.** **Settings → Group outlines → Auto-group orbs by** groups orbs by Directory (the git repo, with worktrees folded into their main repo), CLI, Claude profile or Account. One group appears per distinct value. Turning it off, or switching attribute, deletes nothing. Groups you made by hand are never changed, and heartbeats and crons stay in their own clusters.
- **Hide an orb.** Right-click any orb and choose **Hide this orb**, or **Hide this orb and its team** on a team lead. The session keeps running and the tray still lists it, marked "(hidden)". **Settings → Hidden orbs** lists every hidden orb, so you can bring one back.
- **Clickable links in chat.** Markdown links, bare URLs and `<https://…>` links in chat bubbles now open in your browser. Hovering shows where the link goes. Only http and https links ever open; anything else is shown as plain text.
- **Re-open an OpenClaw conversation.** The New Chat dialog's OpenClaw row now offers **Open existing** beside **New conversation**. It lists the gateway's conversations, including older ones that have no orb, and you can filter them by agent and search them.

## What's fixed

- **Answering from the phone on narrow tmux panes.** A Claude Code session in a narrow pane now reads as at its prompt, so the phone can type into it. Question forms whose options wrap, or that are taller than the pane, now reach the phone and the desktop with the right labels.
- **tmux sessions launched from the app.** Without a UTF-8 locale, tmux mangled the client listing. That made New Chat and orb clicks open a new terminal window instead of attaching to the tmux session that was already open.
- **Cloud session replies.** After you send to a cloud session, the open chat panel now shows the reply.
- **Tables in chat.** Box-drawing listings, pipe tables and ASCII-bordered tables are now drawn unwrapped in a monospace font, and wide ones scroll sideways, so their columns stay lined up.
- **The peer link no longer freezes, or piles up connections.** The machine's certificate is now loaded once instead of on every handshake. On macOS, a keychain prompt could stall that load and silence the whole link. When it recovered, dozens of duplicate connections were opened at once.
- **Respawned teammates keep their persona.** A team member restarted as `name-2` now keeps its own face instead of showing the lead's.
- **Group outlines after hiding the app.** A group outline that was mid-animation when the app was hidden no longer stays frozen in its old shape when the app comes back.

## Upgrading

- Install 1.0.6 from the update notice, or by hand as usual.
- **macOS:** if your other machines, OpenClaw or the phone relay stop connecting after the upgrade, re-grant Local Network in **System Settings → Privacy & Security**.

## Known limitations

- The iPhone app isn't publicly available yet, so the phone features need a test build.

## Which file do I want

| Platform | Download |
| --- | --- |
| macOS, Apple silicon (M1 and later) | `Orbweaver-1.0.6-osx-arm64.dmg` |
| macOS, Intel | `Orbweaver-1.0.6-osx-x64.dmg` |
| Windows 10/11, 64-bit | `Orbweaver-1.0.6-win-x64-setup.exe` |

The `OrbweaverSpeech-*.zip` files are the optional neural speech engine. The app downloads the one it needs, so you don't need to.
